identity.title: Standard Air Contaminant Discharge Permit
identity.issuer: Oregon Department of Environmental Quality, Northwest Region

scan.summary: This is an Oregon air permit issued by DEQ authorizing Cascade Specialty Chemicals to operate two wet scrubbers and solvent storage tanks with vapor control at its Portland facility. The permit specifies operating conditions, monitoring requirements, and reporting obligations. It is a state permit with no gaps—permits are agency documents; compliance means meeting its conditions and renewing on time.
scan.freshness_note: Permit expires November 15, 2026. Today is September 25, 2026. Renewal application was due July 18, 2026 (120 days before expiry per condition 1.3). The company is now past the renewal deadline and operating under the terms of the current permit pending DEQ action on a renewal application, if one was timely filed.

scan.confidence_notes: High confidence on the document's content, dates, and conditions. The permit itself is the agency's document and contains no defects to judge. However, critical concern: the renewal application deadline of July 18, 2026 has passed (today is September 25, 2026). The company must have submitted a timely and complete renewal application by that date to lawfully continue operating. Condition 1.3 states that if a timely and complete renewal application is submitted, the company may continue operating under the current permit until DEQ takes final action. Verify whether a renewal application was submitted by July 18, 2026 and whether DEQ has taken final action. If no timely renewal was filed, operation after the expiration date is a violation. The permit expires November 15, 2026—less than two months away. Certainty on all other condition interpretations is high. No web search was necessary; air permit structure and Oregon DEQ procedures are well established.
